boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Clarkson University
boards.description: Discover the essential late-night food stops for Clarkson University students in Potsdam, from on-campus 'Late Knight' dining to local pizzerias and 24-hour convenience hubs.

cards.title: Late Knight at the Servery
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Dining Hub
cards.notes: Head to the second floor for 'Late Knight' service until 11:30 PM. It is the primary campus spot for late-night tacos, burgers, and breakfast bars during the semester.
cards.short_summary: The central on-campus dining location offering dedicated late-night meal service for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center Servery offers 'Late Knight' dining from 8:30 PM to 11:30 PM, Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:30 PM daily during the academic year; accepts meal plans and Knight Cards.

cards.title: The Famous Pizza Roll Run
cards.subtitle: Downtown Potsdam Staple
cards.notes: Visit this local landmark for their signature deep-fried pizza rolls. It is a long-standing tradition for students heading into downtown Potsdam.
cards.short_summary: A historic downtown pizzeria famous among Clarkson students for its unique deep-fried pizza rolls.
cards.evidence_claim: Sergi's Italian Restaurant has been a family tradition in Potsdam since 1967, serving signature pizza rolls and Italian dishes.
cards.access_notes: Located downtown; check seasonal hours for late-night weekend service.

cards.title: Ice Cream and Snacks at Stewart's
cards.subtitle: Maple Street Convenience
cards.notes: Stop by for a late-night scoop of Philly Vanilla or a quick snack. This regional favorite is a reliable stop for students living near the hill campus.
cards.short_summary: A regional convenience store chain known for its local milk, ice cream, and quick hot food options.
cards.evidence_claim: Stewart's Shops at 26 Maple Street provides convenience items, snacks, and an ice cream counter for the Potsdam community.
cards.source_title: Convenience Store and Gas Station in Potsdam, 13676 | Stewart's Shops - 370
cards.access_notes: Open daily with late hours; features a walk-in ice cream counter.

cards.title: Late Night Slices at Little Italy
cards.subtitle: Market Street Pizzeria
cards.notes: Grab a slice or a 'Sandstoner' sub at this downtown spot. It is a frequent destination for students seeking classic New York-style pizza late into the evening.
cards.short_summary: A popular downtown pizzeria offering New York-style slices and specialty sandwiches.
cards.evidence_claim: Little Italy on Market Street is open until 10:00 PM on Fridays and Saturdays, serving pizza by the slice.
cards.source_title: Contact Us - Little Italy Potsdam NY
cards.access_notes: Open until 10 PM on weekends; offers delivery within the village.

cards.title: The Market Street Taco Run
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Fast Food
cards.notes: A standard late-night destination on Market Street for burritos and tacos. It remains one of the few consistent late-night drive-thru options in the village.
cards.short_summary: A reliable fast-food chain location on the main commercial strip in Potsdam.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell at 153 Market Street serves the Potsdam area with late-night dining hours.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell® in Potsdam, NY - 153 Market Street
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru typically open later than dining room; check app for current closing times.

cards.title: Midnight Golden Arches
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Drive-Thru
cards.notes: Located further down Market Street, this is the go-to for 24-hour service when everything else in town has closed for the night.
cards.short_summary: The primary 24-hour food option in Potsdam, located on the northern end of Market Street.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald's in Potsdam at 171 Market Street offers 24-hour drive-thru service for late-night needs.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is open 24 hours; dining room hours are more limited.

cards.title: The 24/7 Market Street Hub
cards.subtitle: All-Night Convenience
cards.notes: Grab a Slurpee or hot snacks at any hour. This location serves as a critical 24/7 resource for students pulling all-nighters or returning late to campus.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store providing snacks, drinks, and basic groceries on Market Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The 7-Eleven at 147 Market Street is a 24-hour convenience store serving the Potsdam area.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

cards.title: Dinner at RoBro
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Eatery
cards.notes: While it closes earlier than the Servery, RoBro is the heart of campus dining. Check for special late-night themed events like 'Late Knight Breakfast' during finals.
cards.short_summary: The main all-you-care-to-eat dining hall on the Clarkson hill campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Ross-Brooks (RoBro) is the resident dining hall on campus, offering rotating menus and special dining events.
cards.source_title: Dining on Campus & Catering | Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Regular dinner service ends at 8:30 PM; check for special late-night event announcements.

cards.title: Coffee Runs on Maple
cards.subtitle: Early and Late Caffeine
cards.notes: Located in the Mountain Mart, this is the primary spot for a late-afternoon or early-evening caffeine boost before a long study session.
cards.short_summary: The sole remaining Dunkin' location in Potsdam, providing coffee and baked goods.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dunkin' at 119 Maple Street is located within the Mountain Mart and serves the Potsdam community.
cards.source_title: Dunkin' at 119 Maple St in Potsdam | Coffee & Donuts Near You
cards.access_notes: Open until 8:00 PM daily; convenient for students on the eastern side of campus.

cards.title: Riverside Dining at Jake's
cards.subtitle: Hannawa Falls Destination
cards.notes: A short drive from campus, this spot offers brick-oven pizza and a scenic view of the Raquette River. It's a popular choice for a more relaxed evening meal.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront restaurant near Potsdam known for its contemporary cuisine and scenic views.
cards.evidence_claim: Jake's on the Water is located in Hannawa Falls and offers brick oven pizza and contemporary dining.
cards.access_notes: Located about 10 minutes from campus; check seasonal hours for evening service.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional hubs and quiet retreats where Clarkson students actually spend their time, from high-tech labs to riverside trails.

cards.title: Innovation Hub at the ERC
cards.subtitle: Educational Resources Center
cards.notes: Access 3D printers and prototyping tools in this collaborative hub. It is a central spot for engineering students to bring class projects to life outside of formal lab hours.
cards.short_summary: A student-accessible makerspace within the ERC for prototyping and creative projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The ERC houses the Clarkson Ignite and Makerspace, serving as a primary place for students to meet and work with modern technology.
cards.source_title: Clarkson University Campus Tour: Educational Resources Center!
cards.access_notes: Open to the Clarkson community; specific equipment may require training or reservations via the EMS system.

cards.title: The Student Center Forum
cards.subtitle: Student Center Ground Floor
cards.notes: Sit on the tiered 'stairwell' seating for casual study or to watch events on the massive video wall. It is the social heart of the building between classes.
cards.short_summary: A tiered, innovative auditorium space used for both casual lounging and large-scale student events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Forum is an innovative auditorium in the form of a stairwell equipped with a massive video wall, used for lectures, movies, and student connection.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during Student Center operating hours; often used for late-night student events.

cards.title: Riverside Munter Trail
cards.subtitle: Raquette River Bank
cards.notes: Walk this 1.4-mile packed sand trail for views of the Raquette River. It features boardwalks and picnic sites perfect for a quiet break from the engineering labs.
cards.short_summary: A scenic riverside trail managed by the university, popular for walking and outdoor study breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Munter Trail is a wide, level, packed sand trail that follows the Raquette River from the Maple Street Bridge to Bayside Cemetery.
cards.source_title: Munter Trail - St. Lawrence County Trails
cards.access_notes: Open year-round for walking, jogging, and biking; no fees required.

cards.title: Adirondack Outdoor Lodge
cards.subtitle: South Campus Woods
cards.notes: Visit this rustic lodge for Outing Club meetings or to warm up after cross-country skiing. It serves as a wireless internet zone in a wooded setting.
cards.short_summary: A rustic campus lodge serving as the hub for outdoor recreation and student outing clubs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Outdoor Lodge is open 10am to 10pm daily during the academic year for students, faculty, and staff, and serves as a wireless internet zone.
cards.access_notes: Open 10 AM to 10 PM daily during the academic year for the university community.

cards.title: Snell Hall Study Hub
cards.subtitle: Bertrand H. Snell Hall
cards.notes: Grab a coffee and find a table in the open areas of Snell Hall. It is a favorite spot for business and arts students to collaborate between lectures.
cards.short_summary: A popular academic building lounge featuring a coffee shop and collaborative study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Snell Hall features areas for 3D printing, conference rooms, and MoJoe Coffee, housing the School of Business and School of Arts & Sciences.
cards.source_title: A Look Inside Bertrand H. Snell Hall at Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; MoJoe Coffee hours vary by semester.

cards.title: Free Play Game Room
cards.subtitle: Student Center Ground Floor
cards.notes: Challenge friends to pool, darts, or bubble hockey. All games in this traditional lounge are free for student use, making it a top spot for evening downtime.
cards.short_summary: A recreational lounge offering free billiards, darts, and table games for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The ground level of the Student Center features a traditional game room with Pool, Darts, Foosball, Bubble Hockey and Ping Pong games all free for student usage.
cards.access_notes: Open during Student Center hours; equipment typically checked out with a student ID.

cards.title: ERC Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Educational Resources Center
cards.notes: Reserve a room via the EMS system for group projects or quiet focus. These rooms are equipped with iPads to show real-time availability and reservations.
cards.short_summary: Reservable private and group study rooms located within the main university library hub.
cards.evidence_claim: All spaces available for reservation in the ERC can be found in the University EMS system; rooms are equipped with iPads displaying reservation status.
cards.access_notes: Reservations are limited to 2 hours at a time to ensure equal access for all students.

cards.title: Cheel Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Cheel Campus Center
cards.notes: Work out in this modern facility located right inside the hockey arena complex. It is a high-energy spot for students to stay active between classes.
cards.short_summary: A modern student fitness facility integrated into the Cheel Campus Center and Arena.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cheel Campus Center renovation added a new fitness facility, the Steven J. Yianoukos '72 Fitness Center.
cards.access_notes: Open to students with valid university ID; hours vary by season and game days.

cards.title: Science Center Corridors
cards.subtitle: Cora and Bayard Clarkson Science Center
cards.notes: Find a quiet nook in the glass-walled corridors of the Science Center. The third floor near the Internet Teaching Lab is a known spot for focused work.
cards.short_summary: Quiet corridor study spaces with natural light located in the main science academic building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science Center features an Internet Teaching Lab (ITL) with a glass corridor wall on the third floor, used for academic activities.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during academic building hours; elevator access available at the center of the building.

cards.title: Downtown Sim Lab
cards.subtitle: Clarkson Hall (Downtown Campus)
cards.notes: Explore the 'Smart Home' simulation lab used by Health Sciences students. It includes a fully functioning kitchen and living room for practical training.
cards.short_summary: A state-of-the-art health sciences simulation facility located on the downtown campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sim Lab in Clarkson Hall consists of a fully functioning kitchen, bathroom, and living room with integrated smart home technologies.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for Health Sciences graduate students; tours or specific access may be requested through the department.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Clarkson University, from riverside trails and campus game rooms to community parks in Potsdam.

cards.title: Walk the Munter Trail
cards.subtitle: Riverside Nature Path
cards.notes: Stroll along the Raquette River on this 1.4-mile sandy path. It features boardwalks and picnic spots, perfect for a quiet break between classes.
cards.short_summary: A scenic riverside trail managed by the university with public access for walking and fishing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Munter Trail is part of Clarkson University's trail system and is open to the public with no fees.
cards.source_title: Munter Trail - St. Lawrence County Trails
cards.access_notes: Accessible from the rear of the Stewart's Shop on Maple Street or behind the Walker Center.

cards.title: Play Free Table Games
cards.subtitle: Student Center Ground Level
cards.notes: Challenge friends to pool, foosball, or ping pong. These traditional games are located on the ground floor and are free for student use.
cards.short_summary: A social hub in the Student Center offering free billiards and table games for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: The ground level of the Student Center features pool, foosball, and ping pong games that are free for student usage.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during building hours; typically late-night access until midnight or later during semesters.

cards.title: Explore the Back 40 Woods
cards.subtitle: Campus Forest Network
cards.notes: Hike or bike through 400 acres of campus forest. Visit the Bill Vitek Observation Deck to spot local wildlife at the beaver pond.
cards.short_summary: A large on-campus wooded area featuring extensive trails for hiking, mountain biking, and cross-country skiing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clarkson Woods or 'Back 40' is a 400-acre forest on campus with trails open to the public year-round.
cards.access_notes: Trails are open to the public at all times of the year.

cards.title: Study at the ERC
cards.subtitle: Campus Hub & Library
cards.notes: Find a quiet corner or a group table in this central hub. It offers modern study spaces and is the primary academic social center.
cards.short_summary: The main university library and student success hub offering various free study and collaboration environments.
cards.evidence_claim: The ERC offers many spaces where students can meet with peers to do schoolwork with modern technology.
cards.access_notes: Open to students 24/7 with ID card access; public access during daytime business hours.

cards.title: Relax at Ives Park
cards.subtitle: Downtown Riverside Park
cards.notes: Enjoy river views from the gazebo or use the public kayak launch. This park is a popular spot for community concerts and outdoor movies.
cards.short_summary: A public park in downtown Potsdam featuring a gazebo, walking paths, and a kayak launch on the Raquette River.
cards.evidence_claim: Ives Park is a public park with a gazebo and kayak launch that can be used by all visitors for free.
cards.access_notes: Public park open daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Warm Up at the ADK Lodge
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Recreation Base
cards.notes: Visit this rustic lodge to warm up after a winter hike. It serves as the base for the Outing Club and offers a cozy social atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A campus facility dedicated to outdoor recreation, providing a social space for students and hikers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Outdoor Lodge is open from 10am to 10pm daily during the academic year for students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Open 10:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily during the academic year.

cards.title: Hang Out on Cheel Lawn
cards.subtitle: Central Campus Green
cards.notes: Join students on the great lawn for frisbee, yoga, or snow sculpture building in the winter. It's the primary outdoor social hub.
cards.short_summary: The large central lawn between Cheel Arena and the Student Center used for various informal student activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Cheel Lawn is a featured location for wellness activities like snow sculpture building and outdoor exercise.
cards.source_title: Featured Locations: Nature Rx - Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Open public outdoor space available year-round.

cards.title: Play Video Games
cards.subtitle: Student Center Lower Level
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of the Student Center to play the latest video game hits. It's a dedicated space for digital gaming.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus gaming lounge equipped with consoles and popular video games for student recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The virtual game room is on the lower level of the Student Center where students can play video games.
cards.access_notes: Available during Student Center operating hours; typically open late for students.

cards.title: Visit Garner Park
cards.subtitle: Downtown Picnic Spot
cards.notes: Relax on bench swings and enjoy views of the Raquette River dams. This small park features unique outdoor musical instruments.
cards.short_summary: A downtown pocket park offering picnic tables, river views, and interactive outdoor musical instruments.
cards.evidence_claim: Garner Park offers picnic areas with tables and bench swings, plus outdoor musical instruments for public use.
cards.access_notes: Located at the end of Raymond Street; open daily to the public.

cards.title: Wander the Pollinator Meadows
cards.subtitle: Campus Nature Sites
cards.notes: Observe local wildlife and wildflowers at these designated meadows. They are ideal spots for nature meditation and quiet study.
cards.short_summary: Designated natural areas on campus maintained to support local pollinators and provide peaceful student spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Pollinator Meadows are located near Riverside Apartments and Moore House for activities like wildlife watching and meditation.
cards.source_title: Featured Locations: Nature Rx - Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus areas accessible to the public and students year-round.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Choose ten distinct study environments. Verify access rules, room or reservation constraints, and the physical affordance that makes each useful. Treat “Claimed by 9am” as editorial framing; never assert crowding or student behavior without evidence.

cards.title: The Main Library Stacks
cards.subtitle: Educational Resources Center (ERC)
cards.notes: Access the back room stacks for quiet individual study. Use the iPad touchscreens on the columns to locate specific reference materials or technical reports.
cards.short_summary: The primary quiet study area located within the Educational Resources Center on the hill campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harriet Call Burnap Memorial Library is the main library located in the Educational Resources Center and offers reference materials and books for checkout.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check library website for specific reference desk and stack access hours.

cards.title: The Forum Stairwell
cards.subtitle: Student Center Ground Floor
cards.notes: Utilize this innovative stairwell auditorium for casual study between classes. It features a massive video wall and comfortable seating for individuals or groups.
cards.short_summary: A tiered, open-concept seating area in the Student Center used for both events and informal studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Forum is an innovative auditorium in the form of a stairwell equipped with a massive video wall, used for study and meetings.
cards.source_title: Clarkson University Student Center Tour - YouTube
cards.access_notes: Open during Student Center hours; may be reserved for large lectures or performances.

cards.title: Collaborative Reservation Suites
cards.subtitle: Educational Resources Center
cards.notes: Book these rooms through the University EMS system for group projects. Each room features an iPad display showing the current reservation schedule.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group spaces in the ERC designed for collaboration, presentation rehearsal, and digital creation.
cards.evidence_claim: Spaces in the ERC are available for reservation through the University EMS system for group collaboration and presentation rehearsal.
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via EMS; priority given to groups using rooms for intended purposes.

cards.title: MoJoe Coffee Lounge
cards.subtitle: Snell Hall First Floor
cards.notes: Study in a social atmosphere near MoJoe Coffee. This space is ideal for School of Business students needing a quick caffeine break between sessions.
cards.short_summary: A cafe-adjacent study area within the 92,000 square foot Snell Hall academic building.
cards.evidence_claim: Snell Hall features areas for conference rooms, MoJoe Coffee, and classrooms designed for distance learning.
cards.source_title: A Look Inside Bertrand H. Snell Hall at Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; coffee purchase is optional for seating use.

cards.title: The CAMP Atrium
cards.subtitle: CAMP Building Entrance
cards.notes: Find seating in the large atrium near the main oval drive entrance. It provides a modern, bright environment for engineering and science students.
cards.short_summary: A spacious, sunlit atrium located at the entrance of the CAMP research and classroom facility.
cards.evidence_claim: The CAMP building features a main entrance with an atrium located on the left as you walk toward the back lecture halls.
cards.source_title: SOAR Location Detail: Clarkson University: CAMP 175
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; typically quietest during late afternoon lab sessions.

cards.title: Commuter Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: ERC First Floor
cards.notes: Use this dedicated space designed specifically for students who live off-campus. It is located near the commuter lockers and academic support offices.
cards.short_summary: A specialized study area for commuter students to use between classes or during weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Potsdam commuter students have access to a dedicated study space at the Student Success Center.
cards.access_notes: Available to all students, with a focus on supporting the commuter population.

cards.title: The Downtown Book Room
cards.subtitle: Clarkson Hall (Downtown Campus)
cards.notes: Visit the downtown campus for a change of scenery. This library supports graduate health programs and offers a quiet environment for focused reading.
cards.short_summary: A branch library located downtown in Clarkson Hall, serving health sciences programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Health Sciences Library is located downtown in Clarkson Hall and supports graduate health sciences programs.
cards.access_notes: Restricted hours; the Book Room is only open when the library is staffed.

cards.entity_name: Cora and Bayard Clarkson Science Center
cards.title: The Purple Couch Lounge
cards.subtitle: Science Center Corridor
cards.notes: Relax on the signature purple couches at the end of the corridor. This lounge area is situated where the main hallway meets the back wing of the building.
cards.short_summary: A casual lounge area with distinctive purple seating located within the Science Center.
cards.evidence_claim: A lounge area with purple couches is located where the end of the corridor meets the corner of the building near room 175.
cards.source_title: SOAR Location Detail: Clarkson University: CAMP 175
cards.access_notes: Open during Science Center building hours; popular for quick breaks between labs.

cards.title: 24/7 TAC Workstations
cards.subtitle: Technology Advancement Center
cards.notes: Access high-speed network workstations in this modern facility. The building is designed to support advanced research and technical learning platforms.
cards.short_summary: A technology-focused study space with 24/7 computer lab access for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Clarkson has computer labs available 24/7, including workstations connected to the high-speed network backbone.
cards.source_title: Office of Information Technology | Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: 24/7 access available with student ID card swipe.

cards.title: The Living Room Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student Center Level 2
cards.notes: Study in the 'living room' of campus with comfortable chairs and tables. This area is reservable for student groups but open for individual use when empty.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable, multi-purpose lounge area on the second floor of the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center features a variety of lounges and spaces with comfortable chairs and tables for studying and relaxing.
cards.source_title: OSL - Student Center Use Policy | Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Open during Student Center hours; check for group reservation notices on the door.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors of downtown Potsdam that serve as the primary off-campus social and commercial hub for Clarkson University students.

cards.title: The Downtown Social Hub
cards.subtitle: Market Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this primary commercial block to find student favorites like Sergi's Italian Restaurant and various local boutiques in the heart of the village.
cards.short_summary: Market Street is the central commercial corridor of downtown Potsdam, hosting numerous restaurants and shops popular with the Clarkson community.
cards.evidence_claim: Market Street is the site of the annual 'First Saturday' event which welcomes Clarkson and SUNY Potsdam students to the community with live music and discounts.
cards.source_title: First Saturday: Welcome Students | Potsdam Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: Public village street accessible 24/7; business hours vary.

cards.title: Local Food and Co-op Finds
cards.subtitle: Elm Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this block for the Potsdam Food Co-op and popular eateries like Burrito Bob's, located just steps from the Raquette River bridge.
cards.short_summary: Elm Street connects the downtown core to the river and features a mix of specialty food markets and student-friendly dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Potsdam Food Co-op is located at 24 Elm Street and provides local, organic food options to the community and students.
cards.access_notes: Public street; Co-op open daily until 8 PM (Mon-Sat) and 5 PM (Sun).

cards.title: The Historic Gateway
cards.subtitle: Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the historic architecture and local services along this major thoroughfare that links the Clarkson campus to the village center.
cards.short_summary: Main Street serves as a primary artery for Potsdam, featuring historic buildings and essential services used by students and residents alike.
cards.evidence_claim: Main Street is a key corridor in the Village of Potsdam, housing the Potsdam Public Museum and providing access to Ives Park.
cards.access_notes: Public village street; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Riverside Recreation
cards.subtitle: Fall Island District
cards.notes: Cross the bridge to this island park for community festivals, river views, and a unique natural setting in the middle of the Raquette River.
cards.short_summary: Fall Island is a distinct geographic district in the Raquette River that hosts community events and provides scenic recreational space.
cards.evidence_claim: Fall Island hosts the annual Fall Island Fiesta, a community event featuring family-friendly activities and local vendors.
cards.source_title: Many kids events planned at Fall Island Fiesta - North Country Now
cards.access_notes: Public park area; accessible during daylight hours.

cards.title: The Arts District
cards.subtitle: Raymond Street Corridor
cards.notes: Discover the local arts scene at the Creative Spirit Community Arts Center, which offers workshops and gallery space for students and locals.
cards.short_summary: Raymond Street is home to the SLC Arts Council and the Creative Spirit Community Arts Center, serving as a hub for local creativity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Creative Spirit Community Arts Center is located at 6-8 Raymond Street and provides art studios and gallery space.
cards.access_notes: Public street; Arts Center open Tuesday-Saturday with varying hours.

cards.title: The Commercial Connector
cards.subtitle: Maple Street Corridor
cards.notes: Find essential retail and pharmacy services like Kinney Drugs on this busy corridor that connects downtown to the northern village limits.
cards.short_summary: Maple Street (Route 11) is a major commercial thoroughfare featuring essential services and retail outlets for the student population.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clarkson Graduate Student Association lists Kinney Drugs on Maple Street as a primary pharmacy resource for students.
cards.source_title: Grocery and Pharmacy – Clarkson University Graduate Student Association
cards.access_notes: Public village street; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Village Green
cards.subtitle: Ives Park District
cards.notes: Relax at this riverside park featuring a gazebo, walking paths, and a canoe launch, located just behind the downtown commercial buildings.
cards.short_summary: Ives Park is a central green space on the Raquette River used for community gatherings, farmers markets, and student recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Ives Park features a public canoe launch and hosts the Potsdam Farmer's Market on Saturday mornings.
cards.access_notes: Public park; open daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: The Collegiate Corridor
cards.subtitle: Pierrepont Avenue District
cards.notes: Walk this scenic avenue to see historic homes and reach the SUNY Potsdam campus, which shares many resources with Clarkson students.
cards.short_summary: Pierrepont Avenue is a residential and institutional corridor that links the two major university areas in Potsdam.
cards.evidence_claim: Pierrepont Avenue is the primary address for SUNY Potsdam and serves as a major pedestrian link between the campuses.
cards.access_notes: Public village street; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Campus Entryway
cards.subtitle: Clarkson Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: This street serves as the formal entrance to the Clarkson University campus and is lined with university-affiliated buildings and offices.
cards.short_summary: Clarkson Avenue is the main gateway to the university, connecting the village streets to the core academic and residential hill.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clarkson University main campus is officially addressed at 8 Clarkson Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Public street and university entrance; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Market Square
cards.subtitle: Depot Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this block for the Market Square Mall and unique local businesses like the Third Wheel Pottery Studio and the Village Diner.
cards.short_summary: Depot Street features a mix of converted commercial spaces and local businesses that offer unique services to the Potsdam community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Third Wheel Pottery Studio and the Village Diner are located on Depot Street within the Market Square Mall area.
cards.source_title: The Third Wheel Pottery Studio - Potsdam Chamber of Commerce
cards.access_notes: Public street; business hours vary.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From the thunderous train whistle at Cheel Arena to the legacy of the Golden Knight, Clarkson University's traditions are forged in the spirit of the North Country and a deep engineering heritage.

cards.title: The 'Let's Go Tech' Rally Cry
cards.subtitle: A legacy of the Clarkson College of Technology
cards.notes: Chant 'Let's Go Tech' during hockey games to honor the university's former name and engineering roots.
cards.short_summary: The primary athletic chant used by students and the Pep Band, referencing the school's history as Clarkson College of Technology.
cards.evidence_claim: The chant 'Let's Go Tech!' reflects the university's legacy as the Clarkson College of Technology and remains a central part of game culture.
cards.access_notes: Best experienced in the student section at Cheel Arena during home hockey games.

cards.title: The Victory Train Whistle
cards.subtitle: A deafening goal celebration
cards.notes: Listen for the authentic, high-decibel train whistle that blasts whenever the Golden Knights score a goal.
cards.short_summary: A loud, authentic train horn mounted in Cheel Arena that sounds for every Clarkson goal and at the start of games.
cards.evidence_claim: The Train Whistle is a horn that sounds when Clarkson takes the ice and when Clarkson scores, located right above the student section.
cards.source_title: HOCKEY TRADITIONS - Pep Band - Clarkson University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Located inside Cheel Arena; active during all home hockey games.

cards.title: The 'Tijuana' Fight Song
cards.subtitle: A student-run musical staple
cards.notes: Watch the Pep Band perform their signature mash-up of 'Song 2' and 'Tijuana' to energize the crowd.
cards.short_summary: The Clarkson University Pep Band's unique fight song, a mash-up of 'Song 2' and their own arrangement called 'Tijuana'.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pep Band's fight song is a mash-up of 'Song 2' and their own 'fight song' called 'Tijuana'.
cards.source_title: HOCKEY TRADITIONS - Pep Band - Clarkson University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Performed by the Pep Band at every home game in Cheel Arena.

cards.title: Cold Out Gold Out Weekend
cards.subtitle: Celebrating the North Country winter
cards.notes: Join the winter festival featuring ice carving, fireworks, and outdoor hockey to celebrate the cold.
cards.short_summary: An annual winter tradition that includes outdoor activities, hockey games, and community events to embrace the cold climate.
cards.evidence_claim: Cold Out Gold Out (COGO) is an annual winter tradition featuring hockey games, fireworks, ice carving, and outdoor skating.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in late January or February across the Potsdam campus.

cards.title: The Phalanx Tapping
cards.subtitle: Clarkson's highest honorary recognition
cards.notes: Attend the University Recognition Day to see new leaders 'tapped' for induction into the Phalanx society.
cards.short_summary: The formal induction process for Clarkson's highest honorary society, recognizing leadership and service since 1929.
cards.evidence_claim: Phalanx is Clarkson's highest honorary society, and members are 'tapped' for membership during spring ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: The ceremony is part of the annual University Recognition Day in the spring.

cards.title: The Convocation Bell Ringing
cards.subtitle: A bookend to the college journey
cards.notes: Listen for the university bell during your first weekend on campus, a sound you'll hear again at graduation.
cards.short_summary: A formal welcome ceremony for new students where the university bell is rung to mark the start of their academic career.
cards.evidence_claim: During Convocation, new students gather in Cheel Arena and hear the Clarkson bell ring for the first time.
cards.access_notes: Held in Cheel Arena during Orientation weekend for all incoming freshmen.

cards.title: The Goldenrod Legacy
cards.subtitle: Colors inspired by a favorite flower
cards.notes: Wear green and gold to represent the university, colors chosen to honor Thomas S. Clarkson's favorite flower.
cards.short_summary: The university's official colors, green and gold, were selected based on the goldenrod flower favored by the school's namesake.
cards.evidence_claim: Clarkson's colors are green and gold, taken from the goldenrod, Thomas S. Clarkson's favorite flower.
cards.access_notes: Visible across campus on banners, athletic gear, and the university shield.

cards.title: The Skating Mascot
cards.subtitle: A knight on the ice
cards.notes: Watch the Golden Knight mascot skate onto the ice before hockey games to lead the team and pump up the crowd.
cards.short_summary: A unique mascot tradition where a student dressed in full knight armor skates during pre-game ceremonies at Cheel Arena.
cards.evidence_claim: The live mascot, the Golden Knight, skates before games, occasionally with a giant flag or hockey stick.
cards.source_title: Clarkson Unveils New Golden Knight Mascot & Athletics Logos
cards.access_notes: Appears at home hockey games in Cheel Arena.

cards.title: The Top Graduate Awards
cards.subtitle: Honoring the university's founders
cards.notes: Observe the presentation of these prestigious awards to the top two students during the Commencement ceremony.
cards.short_summary: The highest academic honors given to graduating seniors, established by the university's founders in memory of their family.
cards.evidence_claim: The Levinus Clarkson Award and the Frederica Clarkson Award are traditionally given to the two top students in the graduating class.
cards.source_title: Clarkson University Senior Nabiha Madre Receives Levinus Clarkson Award
cards.access_notes: Presented annually during the spring Commencement ceremony in Cheel Arena.

cards.title: The Holcroft Legacy
cards.subtitle: The oldest building on campus
cards.notes: Visit the admissions office at Holcroft House to see the historical marker and the fountain that anchors the campus history.
cards.short_summary: The oldest structure on campus, once a family home, now serving as the admissions office and a symbol of the university's founding.
cards.evidence_claim: Holcroft House is the oldest building on campus, built in 1822, and now houses the admissions offices.
cards.source_title: Clarkson University to Unveil Holcroft House Historical Marker
cards.access_notes: Located on the hill campus; the exterior and historical marker are accessible to the public.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Clarkson University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Navigate your first days as a Golden Knight with this sequence of essential orientation events and campus landmarks.

cards.title: Check In and Get Your Keys
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Start your journey at Price Hall to pick up your room keys and orientation packet from Residence Life staff.
cards.short_summary: The primary check-in hub for new students arriving for move-in weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: New students check in at Price Hall between 9am and 1pm on Friday, August 21, 2026, to receive keys and orientation materials.
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled move-in windows; staff available 9am-1pm.

cards.title: Attend University Convocation
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Ceremony
cards.notes: Join your class for the official welcome and Van Sickle Endowed Lecture in the home of Golden Knights hockey.
cards.short_summary: The university's main arena hosting the formal induction ceremony for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: Convocation and the Van Sickle Endowed Lecture take place at Cheel Arena from 2:30-4pm on Friday.
cards.access_notes: Mandatory event for all new students; accessible via Cheel Lawn entrance.

cards.title: Holcroft Knight of Fire
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Tradition
cards.notes: Experience a signature Clarkson tradition featuring a bonfire and the CUB Glowfest to celebrate your first night.
cards.short_summary: A traditional evening bonfire and social event held on the lawn near the Cheel Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Holcroft Knight of Fire and CUB's Glowfest are scheduled for 8:45-11pm on Friday night at Cheel Lawn.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor evening event; open to all new students.

cards.title: Join the Playfair Activity
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Social
cards.notes: Participate in this high-energy icebreaker designed to help you meet hundreds of your new classmates quickly.
cards.short_summary: A massive interactive social event held outdoors to facilitate student networking.
cards.evidence_claim: Playfair is held on Cheel Lawn from 2-3:30pm on the Saturday of orientation weekend.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor event; participation encouraged for all first-year students.

cards.title: Meet the Greeks & Lawn Games
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening Fun
cards.notes: Head to the Quad Lawn to learn about student organizations and enjoy casual games with fellow students.
cards.short_summary: A social gathering on the central campus quad featuring fraternity and sorority life and lawn games.
cards.evidence_claim: Meet the Greeks & Lawn Games are scheduled for 4:30-6pm on Saturday at the Quad Lawn.
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor space; central to the residential quad area.

cards.title: Watch the Scotty Wiese Magic Show
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night Entertainment
cards.notes: End your Saturday with a professional magic and mentalism performance inside the main arena.
cards.short_summary: A featured entertainment event for new students during the first weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: The Scotty Wiese Magic Show is scheduled for 9-10pm on Saturday night in Cheel Arena.
cards.access_notes: Indoor evening performance; student ID may be required for entry.

cards.title: Explore the Raquette River
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning Nature Walk
cards.notes: Take a break from the schedule to walk this 1.4-mile riverside trail that connects campus to downtown Potsdam.
cards.short_summary: A scenic, level sand trail following the Raquette River, maintained by the university.
cards.evidence_claim: The Munter Trail is a 1.4-mile university-maintained trail along the Raquette River used for student recreation.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible trail; open dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Pick Up Your Mail Key
cards.subtitle: Essential Weekend Task
cards.notes: Visit the main floor of the Student Center to secure your mail key and find your new campus address.
cards.short_summary: The hub for student life, containing mailboxes, dining, and administrative services.
cards.evidence_claim: Students pick up their mail keys in the Student Center main floor after moving in.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; mail services typically available during business hours.

cards.title: Photo with the Mascot
cards.subtitle: Campus Landmark
cards.notes: Snap a photo with the life-size bronze Golden Knight sculpture, a gift from the Class of 2011.
cards.short_summary: A bronze sculpture of the university mascot located in the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Golden Knight Bronze Sculpture is a prominent campus landmark located within the Student Center.
cards.source_title: Deposited Undergraduate Students Welcome | Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Student Center; accessible during building hours.

cards.title: Walk to Downtown Potsdam
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Exploration
cards.notes: Explore the local shops and cafes on Market Street, just a short walk or shuttle ride from the hill campus.
cards.short_summary: The main commercial thoroughfare of Potsdam, featuring local businesses and student-friendly spots.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Potsdam tours and visits to local spots like Park Bros. are common orientation activities for new students.
cards.access_notes: Public street; most shops open 10am-5pm on Sundays.
